bluf: Jellyfish is a London based global digital marketing business, founded 2005, offices in the US, Spain, France, Brazil and Australia, ownership not disclosed, that sells media, creative and data wrapped in generative AI to enterprise brands. The record shows it building an agent and AI product stack (Pencil, Share of Model, Social Agents, AI Studios, CEO Agent) and, on 7 Sep 2026, hiring Seun Odeneye as Chief Media Officer EMEA to build an agentic media practice. A rival should know its house contradicts three of four tested lines (no llms.txt, no social pixel, no LinkedIn ads), all 9 clients on record are names only, and Netflix, Apple and Tinder already shop elsewhere.
doing:
The positioning line, an integrated global digital marketing business combining media, creative and data with generative AI so progressive brands move faster and smarter, decodes as a media network selling speed through AI production and agentic buying. The headline claim, quoted as claims, is assets delivered 55% faster with its Pencil AI platform and One Search driving 19% growth across 38 markets on 14% less budget.

AI Automation / Agents alone scores 3: the homepage leads with AI Studios and Pencil, plus Social Agents and CEO Agent. Five core lines score 2: AI Search / GEO (GEO pages bridging SEO and LLM search, and Share of Model tracking what AI models say about brands), Data & Measurement (a data team building ML tools, GA360, and 2025 Google Measurement Awards wins), Paid Search (the One Search case), Paid Social (paid social and TikTok pages, autonomous Social Agents) and Programmatic & CTV (Display, DV360 and CM360, with Now Next Soon and J+ Bidding). SEO, retail media, CRM, content, creator and CRO score 1. Partners on record: Google Cloud (2026 North America Partner of the Year for Training), Google Marketing Platform (DV360, SA360, CM360, GA360), Amazon Ads (Partner Awards winner), Meta Premium Marketing Partner (undated) and Optimizely Opal certified. Proprietary: Pencil, Share of Model, Jellyfish Social Agents, AI Studios, Now Next Soon, J+ Bidding, Agent Shopper and CEO Agent.

AI posture in plain terms: generative production, autonomous social and shopper agents, and an AI brand visibility product; the move read marks P1 making, the only agency in this batch with an audited AI visibility product on record. Pricing signals: none. Moves in date order: 2025 Digiday AI Awards Most Innovative Use of AI by an Agency and Cannes Lions 2025 Silver for the Apple Severance season 2 campaign; 26 Mar 2025 a new look and an AI powered media in-housing platform; 2026 Google Cloud Partner of the Year and AI Ads Optimization and creator intelligence added to Share of Model (year inferred from news order); 29 Jul 2026 the Tinder brand campaign; 7 Sep 2026 the HOKA Run Your City challenge on Strava and the Seun Odeneye hire. Conspicuously absent: a client case index, jobs, an employee count and any Meta or TikTok library reading.
clients:
The Radar files Jellyfish's client type as enterprise and its home market as London, UK, with offices listed in the United States, Spain, France, Brazil and Australia. Verticals: Fashion & apparel, Sportswear, Entertainment & streaming, Travel and Consumer goods.

The needs read counts 9 clients: 0 observed and 9 names only, from 3 press releases, 2 award entries and 4 slugs, so the mix is empty. No item carries a signal the read can code, yet the record around several describes work. Apple's award entry sits beside the Cannes Lions 2025 Silver for the Severance season 2 integrated campaign, a brand and creative signal. A 7 Sep 2026 item has HOKA running the 'Run Your City' challenge on Strava, a social activation. Tinder's slug and a 29 Jul 2026 item name a brand campaign on dumping traditional dating. Heineken France's slug records a Campaign Ad Net Zero 2024 award and bp's an ABEMD award, neither describing the brief; ForRent's slug, 'estudo de caso forrent', names no work. Netflix, Booking.com and BISSELL are bare names from press and award listings. Every need is inferred from a sold mix led by AI Automation / Agents.

Three clients shop: Netflix also sits with instrument, media-monks, labelium and akqa, Apple with work-co and pmg, and Tinder with vaynermedia.

With nothing observed, what the base needs next is a low confidence judgment from the sold mix. Horus places Jellyfish best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers): these entertainment, travel and consumer brands likely buy Share of Model tracking and agentic media from it next. Under KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two), its main exposure, it is a roughly even chance they press it on paid social and programmatic prices.
house: Say and do: 1 of 4 tested lines practised on its own house. Paid Search is corroborated: the Transparency Center shows 113 ads, 86 in the last 30 days, 97 text and 16 video, under JELLYFISH ONLINE MARKETING LTD and Jellyfish Digital Australia Pty Ltd, last shown 2026-09-27. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility, including Share of Model, and publishes no llms.txt, with 31 AI topic URLs in its sitemap and no AI crawlers blocked. Paid Social is contradicted: no social ad pixel on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: no LinkedIn ads of its own; 1,130 ads match the name query, with the Jellyfish engineering analytics software company and Jellyfish Technologies excluded. Publishing cadence was not tested: the sitemap lists 2184 URLs, 5 updated in 90 days and 108 in 365 days. The tag stack is gtm alone on Nuxt and Prismic, no pixels, test tools or ABM stack. Social links: LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read scores Jellyfish 21.3 on the tailwind index, 74th percentile, band Favored, sold mix at 15:44 on the Solar Arc, afternoon (Ra to Atum), resilience 34.7. Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), carried by AI Search / GEO and Paid Search, and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them), carried by the same two. Most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two), driven by Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV. Best fit: The Bazaar of Agents, 45/100. Moves: P1 and P4 making; P2, P6 and P7 partial; P8 absent; P5 unknown; P3 not applicable.

Monsoon: 46.8, band Breeze, 19th percentile, migration 55.3 against displacement 38.3, so the work could move but the enterprise book does not buy on price. The verdict says 43 of the index is the sold mix, Paid Search (6) and AI Automation / Agents (6) carrying the most movable hours; a delivery footprint is observed in Latin America, with Brazil listed as a hub office; shore 56% South and Southeast Asia, 17% Eastern Europe; automation overlaps 24% of the movable hours. Evidence class observed; no onshore claims.
openings:
The strongest opening is the AI visibility house: Jellyfish sells Share of Model, a product that tracks how AI models describe brands, and publishes no llms.txt on a site with 31 AI topic URLs. A rival whose own site is machine readable can very likely lead with that against the product (moderate confidence: a Nuxt front end may serve the file elsewhere). Falsifier: an llms.txt on jellyfish.com at the next compile.

The book is the second opening: all 9 clients are names only, and Netflix, Apple and Tinder already buy from other tracked agencies, so a rival with described enterprise media cases has proof it does not show in public (likely). Its KJ5 exposure rests on paid social and programmatic hours with no social pixel on its own site, and paid social is where a specialist very likely takes a line. It runs paid search at scale, 113 ads of its own, with no sign of testing ads inside AI assistants, so the first network to show assistant results sets the price. No public pricing model exists, so an outcome priced media offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. Monsoon reads Breeze with displacement 38.3, so a price only pitch is unlikely to work against it; the Brazil hub is the one delivery footprint an onshore pitch can point at.
watch: Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: growth above 15% with AI Mode ads live would confirm S1 and strengthen KJ1, where Jellyfish is best placed.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and pricing below $20 CPM bear on KJ2 and on the assistant ad tests it is not yet making.
Indicator I4, Meta Q3 2026 average price per ad, next reading late October 2026: at or above +5% continues walled garden inflation and deepens KJ5, its main exposure.
The dated move to follow up is the 7 Sep 2026 Seun Odeneye hire to build an agentic media practice; the next Radar compile after 2026-09-28 refreshes ads, sitemap cadence and clients.
